title: An Account of the Polynesian Race, vol. II
author: Abraham Fornander
note: Public domain (London: Trübner). Read in full text with printed page numbers. Fornander counts thirty years to a generation, which puts his pre-contact dates earlier than later reckonings, and his theories of Polynesian origins are long superseded; his summaries of Hawaiian traditions and of the 1770s–1795 wars remain a main open source.

title: Fornander Collection of Hawaiian Antiquities and Folk-lore, vol. IV (Memoirs of the Bernice Pauahi Bishop Museum)

Kamakau's editors point to it for Kūaliʻi's story.
wanted: the rest of the History of Kualii (pp. 364–434): his character and doings, his trip to Hawaiʻi, his return from Molokaʻi, the battle at Kalakoa, and Kauaʻi given over to him, for the kualii event and the Kauaʻi polities of the kakuhihewa era; and the Story of Lonoikamakahiki (from p. 256), with Lono at Kākuhihewa's court and the battle at Waimea where Kamalālāwalu died, for the kakuhihewa and kamalalawalu events
